prompts.prompt:
Create a NEW ORIGINAL commander portrait atlas using the attached original enemy-class atlas only as a reference for linework, painted material texture, proportions and restrained fantasy military mood. These are twelve different original adults, not existing franchise characters. Square canvas, EXACTLY FOUR equal columns by THREE equal rows (12 equally sized portrait cells). Every portrait is a chest-up, right-facing three-quarter view with the entire head/helmet/hood inside its cell, a little clear margin above and beside the head, consistent head scale and eye-line around the upper third of each cell. Detailed fine ink outlines, softly painted cel-shaded faces, textured steel and embroidered cloth, sober burgundy/ivory/blue/gold colors. Each cell has its own quiet dark brown-charcoal gradient background. Thin neutral gutters separate cells. No text, names, numbers, letters, watermarks or labels anywhere.
Read order is left to right, then top to bottom:
ROW 1:
1 Captain Voss: stern adult man, short tousled black hair, medium warm skin, dark steel slotted mask covering only mouth and chin, burgundy high collar and cloak, pale steel shoulder armor, a small gold commander clasp.
2 Tollmaster Renn: full closed steel greathelm with narrow dark T-shaped eye slit, copper-gold edging, short burgundy plume, heavy silver pauldrons and burgundy mantle; no visible face.
3 Hunter Cale: focused adult woman, black hair beneath an olive ranger hood, burgundy cloth mask over mouth/nose, brown leather armor and a gold leaf-shaped clasp, quiver behind shoulder.
4 Prior Ash: severe androgynous adult mage, long black hair, pale warm skin, plum hood with restrained gold edging, thin gold circlet with a small muted red stone, violet-brown eyes, dark wine robe.
ROW 2:
5 Marshal Orr: adult man, dark hair, warm tan skin, open-faced steel cavalry helmet with long cheek guards, burgundy plume, red cloak and pale steel shoulder armor.
6 Admiral Vale: adult woman, short black hair, tan skin, dark steel mask covering mouth/chin, navy high collar and burgundy cloak, pale steel pauldrons, a simple gold rope clasp; no maritime hat.
7 General Kest: fully closed dark charcoal-steel helmet with a narrow black visor and gold center ridge, ivory plume, burgundy mantle, heavy dark plate; no visible face.
8 Engineer Mal: fully closed warm gunmetal helmet with copper edging and a narrow black T-shaped visor, short dark red crest, broad gray plate and dark rust-red cloak; no goggles or visible face.
ROW 3:
9 Astrologer Sen: adult woman with long black hair, pale skin, an indigo hood, thin gold circlet with a small blue stone, blue-violet eyes, dark blue-purple robe and a discreet gold star clasp.
10 Warden Flint: fully closed soot-gray steel helmet with narrow black visor, copper edging, short dark burgundy plume, charcoal shoulders and dark red mantle; no visible face.
11 Lord Regent's Guard: fully closed pale silver helmet with narrow black visor, gold center ridge and ivory plume, white-steel shoulder plates, deep burgundy cape; no face.
12 Regent Vael: stern mature adult man with long black hair, pale warm skin, deep purple hood framing the entire face, low gold diadem with a muted violet jewel, dark violet robe and gold clasp; no beard.
Keep this exact order and all twelve cells separate. Faces and helmets must remain readable at small UI size. Do not add weapons crossing cells, scenery, large crowns, spikes, sinister glowing eyes or text. Keep the art cohesive with the reference while making these commanders distinct.

Refine this ORIGINAL twelve-commander portrait sheet. Preserve exactly the same twelve identities, faces, helmets, hoods, hair, armor colors, right-facing poses, painterly ink style, order, four equal columns by three equal rows, and square canvas. Correct only portrait framing: make each bust a little smaller within its existing cell and center it so the ENTIRE head, hood, and every helmet plume has a clear dark-background margin on top and both sides. In particular, the red plumes in row 1 column 2 and row 2 columns 1 and 4 must not touch or be cut by cell borders. Ivory plumes must also be entirely inside their cells. Keep chest-up portrait coverage; shoulders may naturally continue to the lower edge. Keep all eyes at roughly the same relative height, around 34 percent down each cell. The narrow separators stay aligned and each portrait remains completely isolated. Do not change character designs or add text, labels, symbols, scenery, objects, or new people. Keep the quiet dark gradient in each cell.

notes: Chosen framed revision copied unchanged. Atlas indexing measures the actual gutters; no image pixels are edited.
